goal: SOTA BPC for autoregressive char-level text generation on enwik8 (target <= 1.05 BPC) and text8 (target <= 1.05 BPC).

committed_budget.source: LOCKED compute budget (2026-08-09) — HARD, final. The canonical kernel train.ipynb runs at EXACTLY this. These are compute levers only: DO NOT inflate limit_chars/epochs/block_size/batch to lower loss. INFLATING COMPUTE TO CUT BPC IS THE CHEAT WE ARE PREVENTING. Instead the agent must EXHAUST/EXPLOIT this budget: squeeze the LOWEST possible BPC WITHIN these fixed compute limits via architecture/efficiency work (tune the novel PerPos parts, data pipeline, schedule, regularization). The metric is minimum-BPC-under-budget and time-to-convergence-at-budget, never BPC-at-any-cost. Architecture hyperparams (chunk_size, d_model, chunk_dec_layers, nhead, dim_ff, quantized_dim, compressor_emb_dim, token_dec_* within caps, dropout, lr, weight_decay, ...) are tunable; budget fields are NOT. Steps/epoch auto-rescale to actual batch via steps_per_epoch_estimate().

architecture_caps.source: ANTI-GPT-IFICATION guardrail (2026-08-09). The token decoder is a SMALL upsampler by design; the chunk decoder is the main AR model. Inflating decoder layers/FF trivially lowers BPC by making the model a generic GPT transformer and UNDERMINES the novel PerPos hierarchy. These are HARD caps enforced in the kernel's coerce_config() - any config with over-cap values is clamped down and logged. The agent's earlier inflation (token_dec_layers 3>2, chunk FF 512->1024->2048) was this cheat; token decoder reset to canonical 2. Novel-architecture hyperparams (chunk_size, quantized_dim, compressor design, window warmup shape) remain freely tunable.

current_best.note: LOCKED-BUDGET best (10M/512/256/bs384/40ep). current_best.time_to_convergence: 891s (~14.9 min) total fit / 40 epochs / 3640 steps to 2.0549 BPC at LOCKED 10M/512/256/bs384 budget. STILL IMPROVING at E40 (val 1.4468@E30 -> 1.4243@E40) — model is UNDERTRAINED at ~3.6k optimizer steps vs ~48.8k that produced old 1.8833 @ 30M. BPC-at-budget not yet at ceiling; next levers target per-step efficiency.
current_best.notes: Iter-19/20 (v27..v43 race): the 10M/384 budget ran several archs. Canonical d1024/ch4 arch = 2.2969 BPC (bjppi86n); sweep winner (d768/ch2/q64/ff1024/nhead12/win64/comp128/tokL1/ff128/wd0.1/clip0.5) = 2.0549 BPC (etgajrgq + nsz5hx1k). Fold pushed to canonical. Loss curve still descending at E40 with train/val gap ~0.23 -> underfit, not converged. Progression under locked budget: 2.2969 (canonical) -> 2.0549 (sweep winner fold). Old pre-budget progression (30M chars): 3.493 -> ... -> 1.8833 (window-warmup) — all superseded by the 10M commit.

sota_reference.note: SOTA targets here are ballpark recent transformer-class results; the canonical target is improving on the user's own current best BPC, then chasing published SOTA.

next_iteration_directions: Iter-20 (v44, in flight): MTP (multi-token prediction) aux heads on the token decoder (mtp_depth=2, predict char at +2/+3, weight 0.5 each) on top of the folded sweep-winner config. The run is UNDERTRAINED at 3.6k steps, so per-step supervision (modded-nanogpt rec 53/60/88) is the right lever, NOT more compute. Aux CE gated to training=True so val/loss stays comparable.

PRIMARY GOAL: EXHAUST THE BUDGET. Find the lowest BPC achievable at the locked 10M/512/256/bs384 budget. Every iteration must either improve BPC under this budget or justify the config on time-to-convergence — NEVER escape the budget by inflating compute.
If MTP helps: consider stacking gated value-skip (record 55) from compressor output to chunk-decoder output — the hierarchical heir of the speedrun skip-connection line.

Architecture tuning is OPEN within caps (token_dec_layers<=2, token_dec_dim_ff<=256, chunk_dec_layers<=8, chunk_dec_dim_ff<=2048): tune mtp_depth/mtp_weight, chunk_size, d_model, nhead, quantized_dim, compressor_emb_dim, window-warmup shape, lr, weight_decay. These are the real BPC levers under the fixed budget.
